blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-performance-1 (The export loads the whole audit log into memory and builds the CSV on the event loop) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The handler runs `SELECT * FROM audit_events WHERE org_id = $1 ORDER BY
created_at`, loads the rows into an array, builds the whole CSV string with
`rows.map(toCsvLine).join("\n")`, and sends it.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: Cost grows linearly with the organization's history, per request. The design's own context gives about 40 000 events per organization per month, kept seven years: up to about 3.4 million rows for one export. `query()` in `src/db.ts` returns `result.rows` as one array, so the handler holds every row, then an array of CSV lines, then the joined string, all at once — hundreds of megabytes per request, enough to exhaust the heap or hit V8's maximum string length. `rows.map(...).join` is synchronous: on a service with "one event loop per instance" it blocks every other request of the instance for the whole build. Stream instead: read the rows through a server-side cursor (`pg-cursor` or `pg-query-stream`) in batches, write each batch's CSV lines to the response as they come, and respect backpressure. Replace "Alternatives considered: none" with this alternative and why it is or is not chosen. Ordering (oldest first) and the set of rows stay unchanged.
findings.title: The export loads the whole audit log into memory and builds the CSV on the event loop

findings.evidence: `GET /admin/audit-events.csv` SHALL return every audit event of the organization as CSV, oldest first.
findings.location: specs/audit-export/spec.md#Requirement: Administrators export the audit log
findings.recommendation: The result set grows without limit — up to seven years of events per request — and the requirement allows no way to ask for less: an auditor wanting one quarter still pulls the whole history, holding a database connection and a full scan of the organization's rows for the length of the transfer, and any administrator can repeat it at will. Bound it: add `from` / `to` date parameters (with a default or maximum range) and a scenario for them, or state explicitly that the unbounded export is intended and rely on streaming (R-performance-1) plus a rate limit. This is a separate fix from streaming: streaming bounds memory, not the work per request.
findings.title: The requirement exports every event with no bound on the result set

findings.evidence:
The handler runs `SELECT * FROM audit_events WHERE org_id = $1 ORDER BY
created_at`
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: The schema of `audit_events` is not in the repository, so the index cannot be checked. Without an index on `(org_id, created_at)` the query scans the whole table (every organization's events) and sorts the result, a cost that grows with the total table size, not just the organization's. Check the existing indexes with `EXPLAIN` on a production-sized table, and add a task to create the composite index if it is missing.
findings.title: No index is stated for the export's filter and sort
